Trending:

Oskar Blues Grill & Brew in downtown Denver shuttered at the end of last week.

The restaurant and venue, which is owned by a different group than Oskar Blues’ brewing business, served its last beers and pub fare at 1624 Market St. on Oct. 1, according to a sign posted to its door.

The spot opened off the 16th Street Mall in December 2017. According to Denverite, Oskar Blues signed a 10-year lease at that time for the 10,000 square feet. The restaurant was on the first floor, and 5,500 square feet on the bottom floor was taken by the music and comedy stage, called The Black Buzzard.

Oskar Blues did not immediately return a request for comment from BusinessDen.

“We’re sad to say our Denver location is closed… Thanks for all the good times, Denver!” the sign on its door reads.

In British Columbia, a small award ceremony was held to commend mine operators who continue to monitor and spend on mine reclamation, years after the pickaxes are hung up.

Mining has long been the backbone of Canada’s economy, and BC was the first province to mandate by law that mine plans could only be approved if they had a reclamation operation laid out and budgeted from the start. Reclamation is the industry term for the process of returning brownfield land to productive use, either for farming or forestry, or even for rewilding.

A Denver man’s roommates turned his home into a torture chamber after uncovering his family’s law enforcement ties, launching a brutal ransom plot at the direction of violent Tren de Aragua (TdA) leaders, federal prosecutors said Monday.

The alleged victim survived days of abuse before escaping and walking into a police station missing a finger, prosecutors said.

His captors had recorded the torture and sent the video to his wife, demanding money from his family in Venezuela.

Darwin Veliz-Gonzalez, Jefferson Balza-Delfin and Yender Enrique Campos-Malave, all Venezuelan nationals, were each sentenced to 20 years in federal prison for the kidnapping and torture, the US Attorney’s Office for the District of Colorado announced.

A fourth defendant’s sentencing was postponed.
